title: Sticky positioning constraints
learningObjectives: Explain sticky positioning constraints and use the relevant layout or responsive features.

understand.concept: position:sticky keeps an element in normal flow and offsets it relative to its nearest scroll container when it reaches a specified inset threshold. Sticky behaviour is constrained by its containing block and may not work as expected when the relevant scroll container or available space is misunderstood.
understand.whyItMatters: Sticky elements can cover content or fail to stick if an ancestor's overflow or sizing changes the scroll context. Provide enough room and test nested containers and mobile scrolling.
understand.analogy: A sticky note stays in its section but follows the top edge of the scrolling window until its containing section ends.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual scroll, sizing, and media-query behaviour follows browser layout rules.

explain.narrative: The heading sticks to the top of its scroll container while the content scrolls beneath it.
